bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the 38-Hour Week, Fortnight, and 52-Week Year

When you're offered an hourly rate or a salary, knowing how it translates to annual pay is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, and most calculations assume a 52-week year. This article explains the conversion, including tax, super, and how salary packaging plus can affect your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The simplest way to estimate your annual gross salary is to multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours, then by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, the formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It's a starting point for comparison. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Using the formula:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,260.72 per year (or $1,004.90 per week).

If you're a casual employee, your rate typically includes a 25% casual loading. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour, giving an annual equivalent of $65,325.80. Remember, casual loading is paid in lieu of entitlements like paid leave.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Reference

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply double your weekly pay. For the minimum wage example:

$1,004.90 per week × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight.

This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted fortnightly.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most industries have specific award rates set by the Fair Work Ombudsman, which are often higher. For instance, a retail or hospitality award may specify a higher base rate. Always check your award or enterprise agreement to see if you're entitled to more than the minimum.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% on your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay—it's an additional contribution. For a $52,260.72 annual salary, the super contribution would be $6,271.29, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is separate from any salary packaging plus arrangements, which can further adjust your take-home pay.

### Tax and Medicare in 2026–27

Your annual gross is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For the minimum wage example of $52,260.72, the estimated tax would be around $7,678 (using the 2026–27 scale) plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving a take-home of about $43,537. This is an estimate only—your actual tax may vary with deductions, offsets, or salary packaging plus.

### What About Salary Packaging Plus?

Salary packaging plus refers to arrangements where you sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary for benefits like a car, super contributions, or electronic devices. This can reduce your taxable income and increase your take-home pay, but it also affects your super guarantee base and other entitlements. Our [the timesheet](/) can help you model different scenarios, and you can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) on our site.

### Using the Timesheet for Your Own Rate

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your annual, weekly, and fortnightly gross, plus estimated tax and super. Remember, the calculator assumes a 38-hour week and 52-week year. If your hours differ, adjust accordingly.

### A Note on Averages and Medians

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). This is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. For all employees (including part-time), total earnings average $1,579.20 per week. These figures can give you a benchmark, but your actual pay depends on your role, award, and experience. For more context, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Key Distinctions: Minimum Wage, Award, Casual, and Super

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026).
- **Award rates**: Higher minimums set by the Fair Work Ombudsman for specific industries.
- **Casual loading**: 25% on top of the base rate, included in the $33.05 per hour casual minimum.
- **Super**: 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 cap.

These are the building blocks of your pay. For a deeper dive, visit our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) pages.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
